text:
maria: Quick brain dump — I'm worried about a race between the router releasing a canary lease and the escort process deciding to fallback. We saw a tiny window in staging where requests got sent to both variants for ~200ms. Any ideas on a minimal handshake?
kevin: ugh yeah. saw that earlier. is the lease TTL too short? or is the release path async?
alyssa: Lease TTL was 1s, release is async (fire-and-forget) so the router marks it free locally before remote agent finishes teardown.
maria: Exact. Proposal: make release two-phased — router marks 'draining' with a short guarded grace window (200-500ms) and only flips routing after ack from escort service or after timeout.
samir: +1 to two-phase. We should add an idempotent release token so escort can ignore duplicates.
kevin: We also need to avoid head-of-line blocking. If router waits for ack synchronously, it stalls cutover. Maybe record the drain intent in the control plane and let router continue but tag requests with sticky-header until escort confirms.
alyssa: That would still send traffic to the old variant during graceful drain which we want. But header-tagging is good for observability.
oncall: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for model-v2 on us-west. 50 -> 10 -> 0
maria: Example proto sketch:```
message LeaseIntent {
  string lease_id = 1;
  enum State { ACTIVE=0; DRAINING=1; RELEASED=2 }
  State state = 2;
  int64 expire_ts = 3; // unix ms
}
service Escort {
  rpc UpdateLease(LeaseIntent) returns (LeaseAck) {}
}
```
kevin: With that, router does UpdateLease(DRAINING, expire_ts=now+500ms) and continues routing until Escort returns ACK(RELEASED) or expire. Escort will scatter-backoff and drain active sessions first.
alyssa: Need to handle partial acks from escort cluster — leader election? If only a subset acks, router should treat cluster-level acceptance. Maybe require quorum ack from escort pool for RELEASED.
samir: Quorum is safer but increases latency. Could we use progressive confidence signals: per-node ack -> cluster progress metric -> router uses percentage threshold (e.g., 80%) to flip active routing?
maria: I like percent-based flipping with a hard timeout fallback. That avoids stuck upgrades when one node acts up.
kevin: Observability: emit event stream: lease_intent_created, node_ack, lease_released. We can wire these into rollout checks in Console (health + percent_acked).
alyssa: Edge case: Escort node dies while draining; TTL + automatic node eviction should handle it. We must ensure eviction triggers node_ack=false and counts against quorum/percent.
oncall: oncall: FYI if rollout stalls, ops can force-release via control-plane CLI that flips all leases to RELEASED and triggers immediate fallback. Documented CLI: `ri rollout force-release <lease_id>`
maria: Security note: release token should be signed (HMAC) so malicious router can't spoof RELEASED.
samir: Agree. Also add monotonic nonce to prevent replay.
kevin: Implementation plan: (1) proto + HMAC token (2) percent-ack policy in router config (3) observability events + Console view (4) CLI force-release + RBAC. I can take (1)+(2).
maria: I'll do the Console surface and docs. Alyssa can do escort-side draining logic + node ack semantics. Samir owns security review.
kevin: Quick perf question: how often will UpdateLease be called? Per-cutover only; not per-request. So cost is trivial.
aliysa: small typo: i'm alyssa (two Ls) :)
kevin: lol fixed.
oncall: deploy-bot: Canary progressed: 50 -> 25 -> 5. No anomalies.
maria: Next steps: I'll open an RFC with the proto sketch, percent-threshold options (50/80/100), and a small sim showing worst-case duplicate routing window. Want reviewers: @kevin @alyssa @samir.
kevin: ack, will review.
alyssa: ack, will review.
samir: ack, will review and add threat model notes.
maria: thanks — adding to agenda for architecture sync Friday to align on default percent (leaning 80) and force-release UX.
kevin: TL;DR: two-phase drain + percent-based flip + signed release token + force-release escape hatch.
maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
